examples.ko: 그 사람은 십 년 동안 한 여자만 바라본 일편단심이에요.
examples.en: He is single-hearted; for ten years he has looked at only one woman.

examples.ko: 일편단심으로 남편을 기다리는 이야기가 드라마에 나와요.
examples.en: A story about a wife waiting faithfully for her husband appears in the drama.

examples.ko: 팬들의 일편단심 덕분에 그 가수가 다시 무대에 섰어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the fans' undying devotion, the singer stood on stage again.
He kept his single-hearted devotion to his first love until the end.
My grandfather's lifelong devotion is famous in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 한 팀에만 일편단심인 걸로 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: That player is known for being loyal to just one team.

explain: 사랑뿐 아니라 팀, 회사, 나라처럼 하나의 대상만 향한 변하지 않는 마음에도 써요. 'N에 일편단심이다'처럼 말하고, 일상 대화보다는 드라마나 글에서 조금 문학적인 느낌으로 나와요.
explain_en: It is used not only for love but also for unchanging loyalty to one team, company or country. You say 'N에 일편단심이다', and it sounds a little literary, like something from a drama or a written text rather than casual talk.

examples.en: This restaurant is famous for its delicious à la carte dishes.
I'll order just one dish à la carte instead of the course.

examples.ko: 점심에는 일품요리를 싸게 파는 곳이 많아요.
examples.en: Many places sell à la carte dishes cheaply at lunch.

examples.ko: 일품요리 메뉴에서 먹고 싶은 걸 골라 보세요.
examples.en: Pick what you want to eat from the à la carte menu.

examples.ko: 오늘은 갈비찜 같은 일품요리가 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: Today I want an à la carte dish like braised short ribs.
There are many customers, so à la carte orders are delayed.

explain: 메뉴판에서 '코스'나 '정식'과 나란히 나오는 말이에요. 여러 접시가 차례로 나오는 코스와 달리, 갈비찜이나 비빔밥처럼 한 접시로 식사가 되는 요리를 하나씩 골라 시킬 때 써요. '단품'은 세트가 아닌 메뉴 하나를 가리켜서 쓰임이 가깝지만 똑같지는 않아요.
explain_en: On a menu it appears alongside '코스' (course) and '정식' (set meal). Unlike a course with several plates in order, it is a dish like 갈비찜 or 비빔밥 that works as a meal on one plate and is ordered individually. '단품' (single item) is close in use, but it means one menu item that is not part of a set, so the two are not identical.

examples.en: I swing between joy and sorrow over small things, and it's hard.

examples.ko: 시험 점수 하나에 하는 일희일비는 그만하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to stop swinging between joy and sorrow over a single test score.

examples.ko: 그는 일희일비 없이 늘 담담한 사람이에요.
examples.en: He is always calm, with no emotional ups and downs.
If you reduce the emotional swings, your mind becomes much easier.
I want to get free from the ups and downs over my grades.

examples.ko: 투자할 때는 일희일비보다 긴 안목이 필요해요.
examples.en: When investing, you need a long view more than mood swings over each change.

explain: 보통은 '일희일비하다' 형태로 쓰고, 명사로는 '일희일비가 심하다', '일희일비 없이'처럼 말해요. 주식, 성적, 결과처럼 계속 오르내리는 것 앞에서 '일희일비하지 마세요'라고 충고할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '일희일비하다', and as a noun in phrases like '일희일비가 심하다' or '일희일비 없이'. It fits well when advising someone not to get carried away by things that keep going up and down, like stocks, grades or results.

en: be now glad, now sad; have joy and sorrow in alternation

examples.en: Don't swing between joy and sorrow over small things.
I get happy and sad every time my score goes up and down.
I tend to get carried away by the stock price.
I won't get worked up until the results come out.
My parents don't get emotional over my grades.

examples.ko: 친구는 연애 문제로 하루에도 몇 번씩 일희일비해요.
examples.en: My friend's mood swings several times a day over love troubles.

explain: 'N에 일희일비하다' 형태로 써요. 조언할 때는 '일희일비하지 마세요'처럼 부정형으로 많이 말해요. 기쁨과 슬픔이 번갈아 온다는 느낌이라, 계속 좋거나 계속 나쁜 상황에는 어울리지 않아요.
explain_en: It is used as 'N에 일희일비하다'. When giving advice people often use the negative, '일희일비하지 마세요'. It implies joy and sadness alternating, so it doesn't fit a situation that is just constantly good or constantly bad.

examples.en: The new team leader received the certificate of appointment today.
The name and position are written on the certificate of appointment.

examples.ko: 임명장 받는 날에는 가족이 모두 와요.
examples.en: On the day of receiving the appointment certificate, the whole family comes.

examples.ko: 이 임명장은 액자에 넣어 둘 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to put this appointment certificate in a frame.
An appointment certificate is hanging on the office wall.
I started the work without even an appointment certificate.

explain: '임명장을 받다', '임명장을 주다'와 함께 쓰고, 행사 이름으로는 '임명장 수여식'이라고 해요. 윗사람에게 줄 때는 '임명장을 드리다'라고 높여요.
explain_en: It goes with '임명장을 받다' (receive) and '임명장을 주다' (give), and the ceremony is called '임명장 수여식'. When giving it to a superior, you say '임명장을 드리다'.

examples.en: After eating greasy food, I cleanse my palate with coffee.
I'll go buy some fruit to cleanse our palates.

examples.ko: 매운 걸 먹은 뒤에 냉수로 입가심했어요.
examples.en: After eating something spicy, I rinsed my mouth with cold water.
I ordered cold sikhye to refresh my mouth.

examples.ko: 식사 후에 껌으로 입가심하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people freshen their mouth with gum after a meal.

examples.ko: 입가심하고 싶으면 물부터 한 모금 드세요.
examples.en: If you want to clear your mouth, have a sip of water first.

explain: 'N(으)로 입가심하다' 형태로 쓰고, N에는 물, 차, 과일, 시원한 음료처럼 입안을 개운하게 해 주는 것이 와요. 명사 '입가심'으로도 많이 써서 '입가심으로 과일을 먹다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used as 'N(으)로 입가심하다', where N is something refreshing like water, tea, fruit or a cold drink. The noun '입가심' is also common, as in '입가심으로 과일을 먹다'.

examples.en: We'll stock the new products in the warehouse tomorrow.
I took my car into the repair shop to get it fixed.
I'll let you know as soon as we get the new items in stock.
It's the day the bookstore takes in new books.

examples.ko: 물건을 입고할 때는 먼저 개수를 세어요.
examples.en: When taking in goods, we count the number first.
The store stocked its winter clothes yesterday.

explain: 반대말은 '출고하다'예요. '옷을 입고(입다)'와 소리가 같지만, 가게나 창고 이야기에서는 물건이 들어온다는 뜻이고 자동차를 정비소에 맡길 때도 써요. 물건이 주어면 '입고되다', 사람이 들여놓으면 '입고하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '출고하다' (ship out). It sounds the same as '옷을 입고' (wearing clothes), but in talk about shops and warehouses it means goods come in, and it is also used when you leave a car at a repair shop. With goods as the subject you say '입고되다', and with a person doing it, '입고하다'.

examples.en: Tomorrow is Ipdong, so the weather is chilly.
Now that Ipdong has passed, the morning air is cold.
Many households start making kimchi for winter around Ipdong.
This year Ipdong is around November 7.
Around Ipdong, the first ice sometimes forms.
Some homes turn on the heating from Ipdong.

explain: 24절기 중 하나로, 달력에서 겨울이 시작되는 날로 표시돼요. 보통 11월 초이고, 입춘, 입하, 입추처럼 '입-'으로 시작하는 절기 이름과 함께 알아 두면 좋아요. 날씨 뉴스나 달력에서 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is one of the 24 solar terms and is marked on the calendar as the start of winter, usually in early November. It's good to learn it together with 입춘, 입하 and 입추, the other terms that begin with '입-'. You can see it in weather news and on calendars.

examples.ko: 회사에서 직원에게 돈을 주고 입막음을 했대요.
examples.en: I heard the company paid the employee to keep quiet.
There's a rumor that the money was hush money.

examples.ko: 그 일은 입막음 때문에 알려지지 않았어요.
examples.en: That matter didn't become known because of the silencing.
I gave my little sibling snacks to keep them quiet.
Despite his efforts to silence people, the rumor spread.
Keeping people quiet wasn't easy, so I finally gave up.

explain: 돈, 선물, 부탁, 위협으로 다른 사람이 말하지 못하게 하는 일이라 조금 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 뉴스에서는 '입막음용 돈'처럼 자주 나오고, 가볍게 비밀을 부탁할 때는 '비밀로 해 줘요'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means getting someone not to talk through money, gifts, requests or threats, so it has a somewhat negative tone. In the news you often see it as '입막음용 돈' (hush money), while for a light request to keep a secret people say '비밀로 해 줘요'.

examples.ko: 입바른 소리를 하면 미움을 받기도 해요.
examples.en: If you speak bluntly, you sometimes get disliked.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 입바르게 말해서 가끔 분위기가 어색해져요.
examples.en: That friend speaks so bluntly that the mood sometimes gets awkward.

examples.ko: 저는 입바르지 못해서 윗사람에게 할 말을 잘 못해요.
examples.en: I'm not outspoken, so I have trouble saying what I think to my superiors.
Frankly speaking, this plan is too much.
He states his opinion frankly even to his superiors.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 어릴 때부터 정말 입발라요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has been very outspoken since childhood.

explain: 대부분 '입바른 소리', '입바른 말' 형태로 써요. 틀린 말은 아니지만 듣는 사람이 불편할 수 있는 바른말을 한다는 느낌이에요. '르' 불규칙이라 '입발라요', '입발라서'가 돼요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in the forms '입바른 소리' or '입바른 말'. It suggests saying something that is correct but may make the listener uncomfortable. It is a 르-irregular, so you get '입발라요' and '입발라서'.

examples.ko: 사람들이 그 일로 한참 입방아를 찧었어요.
examples.en: People gossiped about it for quite a while.
Celebrities easily become the subject of gossip.

examples.ko: 작은 마을이라 소문이 나면 입방아가 심해요.
examples.en: It's a small town, so gossip is intense once a rumor starts.

examples.ko: 남의 입방아는 신경 쓰지 말고 자기 길을 가세요.
examples.en: Don't mind what others gossip about and go your own way.
I suffered a lot because of the gossip.
He stayed firm despite the neighbors' gossip.

explain: '입방아'는 남의 이야기를 이러쿵저러쿵 말하는 것을 가리키고, 보통 안 좋은 느낌이에요. 그냥 '소문'이나 '이야기'보다 사람들이 입에 올리며 떠든다는 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.example: 그 커플이 한동안 사람들 입방아에 올랐어요.
phrases.en: That couple was the talk of the town for a while.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 계속 이야기하는 대상이 된다는 뜻이에요. 보통 좋지 않은 일로 말이 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means becoming the subject people keep talking about, usually for something not so good.
phrases.en_equiv: be the talk of the town

phrases.en: Don't gossip about other people's business.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 이야기를 이러쿵저러쿵 떠든다는 뜻이에요. 방아를 찧는 것처럼 입을 계속 움직인다는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means to chatter about other people. The image is of the mouth moving nonstop like pounding in a mill.

explain_en: It refers to people talking about someone else this way and that, usually with a negative feel. Compared with plain '소문' (rumor) or '이야기', it strongly suggests people keep chattering about the person.

en: way of speaking; being in the habit of saying things a certain way

examples.en: My grandmother says 'Health comes first' like a catchphrase.
Saying he's tired is a habit of that friend.

examples.ko: 입버릇으로 하는 말이니까 신경 쓰지 마세요.
examples.en: It's just something he always says, so don't mind it.
It's good to fix a bad speaking habit.
'Let's go together later' was my dad's usual line.
When I changed what I habitually say, my mood got better too.

explain: '입버릇처럼 말하다'로 가장 많이 써요. 같은 말을 습관적으로 자꾸 하는 것을 말하고, '말버릇'과 비슷하게 쓰여요. 진심이라기보다 습관처럼 나오는 말이라는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: The most common use is '입버릇처럼 말하다'. It describes saying the same thing again and again out of habit, and it is used much like '말버릇'. It carries a sense that the words come out by habit rather than from real feeling.

examples.en: Prize money is given to the prizewinners of the contest.
The list of prizewinners is posted on the website.
Among this year's prizewinners, there is even an elementary school student.
The prizewinners are invited to the award ceremony next week.
Unfortunately, I didn't make it among the prizewinners.
Everyone was nervous on the day the prizewinners were announced.

explain: '입상하다'(상위에 들어 상을 받다)와 짝으로 알아 두세요. '우승자'는 1등을 가리키지만 '입상자'는 등수 안에 들어 상을 받은 사람들을 두루 말해요. 대회, 공모전, 시상식 이야기에서 자주 써요.
explain_en: Learn it as a pair with '입상하다' (to place and win a prize). '우승자' refers to the first-place winner, while '입상자' covers everyone who placed and received a prize. It is used often when talking about contests, competitions and award ceremonies.

examples.ko: 그 아저씨는 입심이 좋아서 늘 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: That man is a great talker, so he's always popular.

examples.ko: 입심 좋은 사회자 덕분에 행사가 재미있었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the smooth-talking host, the event was fun.
Nobody can beat my grandmother's gift of gab.
Some broadcasters make a living with their way with words.

examples.ko: 그 가이드는 입심도 좋고 아는 것도 많아요.
examples.en: That guide talks well and also knows a lot.

examples.ko: 입심만 믿고 준비 없이 발표하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't present without preparing, relying only on your talking skills.

explain: 보통 '입심이 좋다', '입심이 세다'처럼 말해요. '입담', '말솜씨'와 비슷하게 쓰이는 구어적인 말이고, 말을 막힘없이 잘한다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is usually said as '입심이 좋다' or '입심이 세다'. It is a colloquial word used much like '입담' or '말솜씨', and it suggests speaking fluently without hesitation.

examples.ko: 낚시를 시작한 지 한 시간 만에 입질이 왔어요.
examples.en: A fish bit an hour after I started fishing.

examples.ko: 오늘은 입질도 없어서 한 마리도 못 잡았어요.
examples.en: There wasn't even a bite today, so I didn't catch a single fish.
When you feel a bite, pull the fishing rod slowly.
The fish only nibbled and swam away.
Bites come most often in the morning.

examples.ko: 입질 시간대를 알면 낚시가 더 재미있어요.
examples.en: If you know when the fish bite, fishing is more fun.

explain: '입질이 오다', '입질이 없다'처럼 써요. 물고기가 미끼를 건드리기만 해도 입질이라서, 입질이 왔다고 꼭 잡은 건 아니에요. 낚싯대를 당겨 바늘에 걸리게 하는 동작은 따로 '챔질'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used in phrases like '입질이 오다' (get a bite) and '입질이 없다' (no bites). A fish only touching the bait already counts as 입질, so a bite does not mean you have caught it. Pulling the rod to set the hook is called '챔질'.
